### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e05ed1ec2ecce09b19a23bd51a6f14afb40caf3`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e05ed1ec2ecce09b19a23bd51a6f14afb40caf3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `34d76d06de6955c1165ba12bab5da21d980e97a9` — the merge of head `7e37e4c238a4b6c748ff0ae1466b01e2d80680a4` into base `3e05ed1ec2ecce09b19a23bd51a6f14afb40caf3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 34d76d06de6955c1165ba12bab5da21d980e97a9 && git checkout 34d76d06de6955c1165ba12bab5da21d980e97a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3e05ed1ec2ecce09b19a23bd51a6f14afb40caf3 7e37e4c238a4b6c748ff0ae1466b01e2d80680a4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3e05ed1ec2ecce09b19a23bd51a6f14afb40caf3 && git merge --no-ff 7e37e4c238a4b6c748ff0ae1466b01e2d80680a4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e05ed1ec2ecce09b19a23bd51a6f14afb40caf3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3e05ed1ec2ecce09b19a23bd51a6f14afb40caf3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7e37e4c238a4b6c748ff0ae1466b01e2d80680a4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.adopt-orphans-owner-judges.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-adopt-orphans-object-registry.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-owner.ts (`classifyObjectContribution`, `releaseAdoptedObjectOwner`), packages/spec/src/security/permission-set-owner-binding.ts (`judgePermissionSetOwnerBinding`), packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts (`ReassignOrphanedMetadataResponseSchema`), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the `adopt-orphans` route), packages/qa/dogfood/test/package-first-authoring.dogfood.test.ts (the D5 adopt pin), docs/adr/0029 D9.9, docs/adr/0086 D3, docs/adr/0146 D10 and D11, docs/adr/0070 D5

Read at 2026-11-01T22:37Z: card #28776 (body and all 4 comments: the claim `6562862818`, the step-1 ruling `6563043440`, the two os-dev-reports `6563905031` and `6564870922`), PR #28808 (body, 5-file list, the net diff `origin/main...7e37e4c2`; merge-base `c9a9981d`, mergeable clean), and the 48 check-runs on the head. The changeset `.changeset/28776-adopt-orphans-owner-judges.md` is a prose face: read for ②, not reviewed. The pinned ledger is generated output (`check:engine-double-contract --write`): not reviewed. Scope widened over the floor to the cited code and the spec faces named above.

**Check-runs on `7e37e4c2`** (read 2026-11-01T22:37Z): 48 total, all `completed`, none in progress. 34 `success`, 14 `skipped` (the opt-in harnesses, the UI build/lint/typecheck/test matrix, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, the dogfood shard matrix, the schedule-gate skip: none applies to a diff with no `ui/`, docs or spec file). Green and material to this diff: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 (7/8 at 22:22Z, the `df5ce323` red cleared), Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint & Repo Gates with every scoped lint family, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, Type Check · workspace, debt ledger, source and consumer gates, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Live E2E UI. The conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was run here.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff moves one method, `reassignOrphanedMetadata` (`POST /api/v1/packages/:id/adopt-orphans`), and no public surface. Each accept-set change it implies, judged in the tree:

1. **An ACTIVE orphan `object` row whose name a package other than the target owns in the registry is refused whole, `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` / 422.** Right. `classifyObjectContribution` (protocol-object-owner.ts) answers `mismatch` for binding T against owner O when T is not O, on both the packaged-owner and the runtime-owner branch; the adopt loop calls it with `request.targetPackageId` before the first `engine.update`, so the refusal precedes every write and `applyRegistryWriteThrough`. The envelope is `overlayPackageMismatchError(name, T, O)`, the save door's own (status 422, code, `packageId`, `ownerPackageId`, the "Cannot layer object" sentence). On `main` the same row was rebound in storage, `releaseAdoptedObjectOwner` answered `false` (owner not the sentinel), and the registry kept O: the `P == Q` row ADR-0029 D9.9 says is "refused at the producer, loudly" and that `loadMetaFromDb` counts as an error at the next boot. The route relays `.status` and `.code` (`errorFromThrown` reads `.status` first), so the wire answer is 422, as the objectql kernel pin reads it.
2. **The `'sys_metadata'` sentinel owner is excluded from that arm.** Right, and load-bearing. An orphan object's own registration is under the sentinel (#23514, #23646), so `classifyObjectContribution(name, T)` answers `mismatch` with owner `sys_metadata` for every plain orphan; judged unchanged, the door would refuse every object adoption and ADR-0070 D5's convergence door would be dead (the step-1 measurement showed exactly that on a real CRM boot). The sentinel is "no package" (ADR-0070 TL;DR 1; `overlayPackageMismatchError` itself routes a sentinel owner to a different refusal). The exclusion is pinned by the sentinel CONTROL (a sentinel-owned and an unowned orphan both move, `reassignedCount: 2`) and ablated (3 red with the exclusion off). Nothing else can answer `mismatch` with the sentinel: only the runtime-owner branch does, and only when `getObjectOwner` answers it.
3. **An ACTIVE orphan `permission` row whose body `packageId` disagrees with the target is refused whole, `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, `issues[0].path = 'packageId'`.** Right. `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal(type, body, name, T, 'save')` is the save door's envelope around the one judge (`judgePermissionSetOwnerBinding`, packages/spec/src/security), called with the binding the row lands in, which for an adoption is the target, exactly as the save door passes `saveWriteBinding` and the promotion passes `promoteInto`. ADR-0086 D3's verdict table: declared `'Q'` against bound `'P'` is refused, "never silently overridden". On `main` the adoption rebound the row into T while its body still said X: the silent override D3 exists to refuse. An absent key passes; a body naming the target passes (CONTROL pinned). An empty-string `packageId` is refused against any target, the judge's own fourth row, consistent with the save door.
4. **Order: owner judges, then the `__c` judge.** Right against the save door: there the D9.9 object judge (protocol.ts, the `classifyObjectContribution` block) and the permission owner judge both precede `objectBodyExtensionFieldSuffixRefusal`; here the one owner loop precedes the `judgeExtensionFieldSuffix` block. Pinned: a row both judges refuse answers 422, not 400. One difference, noted and not a defect: the save door judges one item per request, so there is no cross-type order to copy; the adopt door judges rows in read order and throws on the first, so a multi-row adoption reports one owner refusal at a time, while the `__c` judge reports every field in one `issues[]`. The ruling asked for "each judge's existing envelope", which is this; a batched report would be a new envelope.
5. **A draft row is not judged (`row.state !== 'active'` skips it); an unparseable permission body is skipped (`continue`).** Right, and the #23690 / #28735 shape: a draft never reaches the runtime and is judged by both owner judges at its promotion (the publish door at the `promoteInto` block); an unparseable row is rebound as stored, as the `__c` judge and `duplicatePackage` leave it. Neither widens anything.
6. **No public surface moves.** `ReassignOrphanedMetadataResponseSchema` (packages/spec) is unchanged; no export, no spec file, no new error code: both codes are already the save door's, registered to this package. The route is untouched. The dogfood D5 pin (`package-first-authoring.dogfood.test.ts`: a package-less DRAFT object adopted into `app.dogfood_adopt`) stays green by construction, a draft is not judged.
7. **The rewritten objectql control** (`protocol-adopt-orphans-object-registry.test.ts`, the #23646 kernel suite). Judged on its own: it still pins something real, not a flipped expectation. The old CONTROL pinned "rebound in storage, the registry keeps R". The new case boots a real kernel (`ObjectQLPlugin`, the real `SchemaRegistry`), saves R's row through the real save door so `getObjectOwner` answers R by the real path, inserts the package-less residue, and pins three things: the wire shape (422, the code, the message naming R), that storage is NOT rebound (bindings `[R, none]`, so the refusal precedes the update on the real engine, not only on the double), and the #23646 half unchanged (no `registerObject` / `unregisterObject` / object `registerItem`, owner R, the served definition still R's label and package). That is the end-to-end pin the metadata-protocol unit suite cannot give (its registry is a table the test sets). The header's bullet list names the change. The other five cases of the file are untouched.
8. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`**: two `pinned: 1` rows for the new test's `findOne` and `update`, the gate's own `--write` output after the double was routed through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` / `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`. Generated; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` green on the head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (18.2.0): `minor`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reasons, and a migration paragraph. Matches what the diff publishes: a requirement tightened at one more write door is `narrowed`, a kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and carries its disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). The marker's category holds in the tree: no key, value, export or code is removed or renamed and there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; the remedy is an author's choice (bind, delete or rename the object; drop or fix the set's `packageId`). The level and the two lines are byte-for-byte the shape of the #28735 precedent (`c363084b53`, the same door). `Check Changeset` and `check:adr-0087-registration` (in Lint & Repo Gates) green. `Clause-②:` line: `no (narrowing)`, correct: nothing an author can write is widened; the measured count at the base is 0.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` (round 1): the permission arm speaks the spec judge's `'save'` door words ("this save writes it into package T"); A keep, or B a spec card for an `adopt` verb.** Answered **A**. `PermissionSetOwnerBindingDoor` is a closed union in packages/spec (out of this PR's file surface by the claim), the protocol wrapper narrows it further to `'save' | 'restore' | 'publish'`, and the save words carry the right remedy for an adoption: drop the key, or put the set where it declares, then send it again, nothing was written. "This save" names the act loosely for a door with a measured count of 0. Not escalated as a card: a spec verb would be a cosmetic widening of a closed union for a sentence nobody has read on the wire. If a seat wants the exact word, it is a future spec card, not a condition of this PR.
- **Round 2's disclosed deviation** (a parse-error splice left for minutes while the gate loop ran; `check-comment-mask-corpus` read it UNPARSEABLE; fixed in the amended, unpushed commit; 8 overlapped gates re-run). Answered: nothing broken reached the head; `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus` and every lint family are green on `7e37e4c2`.
- **Round 1's miss** (only the metadata-protocol suite run; Test Core 7/8 red on `df5ce323`). Answered by the head: 8/8 shards green, and the moved pin is judged in ① item 7.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[0]`: the namespace-prefix judge at this door.** Escalated, not a gap of this PR: the card's ruling `6563043440` sends refuse / rename-on-adopt / unjudged to the maintainer, and the method header says the judge is deliberately not asked. Carrier: the maintainer; the seat holds it.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[1]`: `releaseAdoptedObjectOwner`'s "another package owns it" row (answers `false`) is no longer reached in the ordinary run.** Accepted as left: the loop `await`s between the judge and each update, so a registry change in between still meets that row, and it fails in the cheap direction (storage rebound, registry untouched, the next boot counts it). Not dead code to delete in this PR.
- **The round-2 `acceptance_notes_addition`** (the moved #23646 pin) is for the seat to add to the PR body; the body's Verification section still reads at `df5ce323`. Body residue, judged below as should-fix for the seat, not of the tree.
- No dev flag is left unanswered. The dev reports `mcp_calls: 0` and the relay writes it names; the card's assignee and labels untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main` and the cited code, with the design tried for breaks:

**Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The published surface for this door is `ReassignOrphanedMetadataResponseSchema` and its docblock: "bulk-rebind package-less (orphaned) metadata into this base (ADR-0070 D5)". D5 promises "Existing `package_id = null` rows are not broken" and a bulk-assign of legacy orphans; it declares nothing about a row the registry cannot hold under the target. The two rows this PR refuses were never deliverable by that promise: the D9.9 row produced "two rows for one object" in storage with the registry still naming the other owner (the shape ADR-0029 D9.9 declares not representable, refused at the producer and counted as an error at boot), and the D3 row produced a set bound to T whose own body says X (the silent override D3 refuses at every door that files a set). So the narrowing **makes the spec's own refusal real** at one more door, rather than narrowing a delivered capability at the consumer. The door still adopts every row the spec can serve: the sentinel CONTROL, the target-owned CONTROL, the two permission CONTROLs, the dogfood D5 draft, and the #23646 kernel adoptions all still move.

**Does it dead-end D5 / D11?** Tried and no. The break would be the sentinel: every plain orphan object is registered under `sys_metadata`, so an unexcluded judge refuses all of them (the step-1 control proved it). The exclusion is explicit, pinned and ablated. ADR-0146 D11 shrinks this door's input (package-less rows of packaged items migrate into `.custom` as declared overrides) but keeps D5's treatment for a package-less row no package ships, which is exactly the row this door still adopts; the judges touch only rows D11 would not migrate either (an object another package owns is not "an item no package ships"). The prefix judge, the one that would dead-end the door, is not asked, by ruling.

**Is the judge asked at the right binding and time?** Yes. The save door's D9.9 block judges "the package the write lands in" and the permission judge "the resolved binding of the row the write lands in"; an adoption lands every row in the target, so `request.targetPackageId` is that binding for both. Both are asked after the orphan read and before the first `engine.update` (pinned: `update` and `applyRegistryWriteThrough` never called on refusal), so a refusal costs no write, and the response schema's `success`/`reassignedCount` are never answered for a partial run; the loop's own per-row refusal channel (#12981) is untouched for the storage-level failures it exists for.

**Could a refused adoption be worked around through another door?** Tried: the save door refuses the same object row naming T (D9.9) and the same set body naming T (D3); the publish door refuses a draft of either at promotion; `duplicatePackage` rewrites a set's `packageId` to the target before its own save. No door admits what this one now refuses. Conversely nothing this door admits is refused elsewhere: a sentinel-owned orphan adopted into T is then registered under T by the write-through, which is the #23646 answer.

**The rewritten control** (brief's question): it pins the real-kernel refusal and the registry invariant together; a flipped expectation would have kept `storedBindings` at `[Q, R]`. See ① item 7.

Findings:

- **should-fix (seat, PR body, not the tree):** add the round-2 Acceptance-notes line (the moved #23646 pin, `protocol-adopt-orphans-object-registry.test.ts`) and a Verification line for `7e37e4c2` (the dev wrote the body once at `df5ce323`; the report gives the text). The body's account is otherwise consistent with the tree.
- **observation, no fix owed:** the adopt door reports one owner refusal per attempt in row read order (see ① item 4). If an environment ever holds more than one refused row, the operator fixes them one adoption at a time. The save door's per-item envelope is what was ruled; a batched `issues[]` would be a new envelope and a new card.
- No must-fix.

Reviewed-by: `session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC`
